                    ### Question
                    An investigator is studying the crossbridge cycle of muscle contraction. Tissue from the biceps brachii muscle is obtained at the autopsy of an 87-year-old man. Investigation of the muscle tissue shows myosin heads attached to actin filaments. Binding of myosin heads to which of the following elements would most likely cause detachment of myosin from actin filaments?

                    ### Options
                    opa. cGMP
opb. Troponin C
opc. ATP
opd. Tropomyosin
ope. ADP

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Detachment of myosin from actin filaments in the crossbridge cycle of muscle contraction most likely requires ATP, as it provides the energy for this process. ADP, through the release of inorganic phosphate, is also involved in this energy transfer. Troponin C, cGMP, and tropomyosin are not directly involved in the detachment of myosin from actin filaments.
